subject: Data path transparency: execution loci, subprocessors, and cross-border triggers
messages:
From: Oliver Stone <oliver.stone@atlantech.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emma Jackson <emma.jackson@atlantech.com>
Date: 2026-09-13T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Initial questions: execution loci, subprocessors, and cross-border triggers

Hi Monica,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. Our security and legal teams have a few follow-ups before we move to procurement: specifically we need clarity on where customer inference requests may be executed (per-region processing), the roster of subprocessors for the EU region, and what conditions would cause an inference request or customer data to transit outside the EU (e.g., capacity failover, maintenance, or vendor fallback).

High level asks:
- Short list of processing sites / regions where Atlantech requests could be executed.
- The named subprocessors involved in request handling, telemetry, and storage for EU customers.
- Specific triggers that would cause cross-border movement and whether we can opt out.
- Retention and deletion timeline for transient runtime artifacts and model caches.

If possible, please attach any evidence pack or a short one-pager that covers the above. Aim is to confirm we can meet our internal data residency commitments.

Cheers,
Oliver
Oliver Stone
Head of Security Engineering
Atlantech Health

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Stone <oliver.stone@atlantech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-13T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial questions: execution loci, subprocessors, and cross-border triggers

Hi Oliver — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers inline, and I've attached a short evidence pack (see attached PDFs). Karthik and Marissa are looped in for pricing/contract and technical fallbacks.

High-level summary:
- Regions/Execution Sites: We run inference in explicit regions: EU (Frankfurt and Amsterdam), UK (London), US (us-east-1), and APAC (Singapore). For EU customers we offer region-pin so requests are routed to the EU pool by default.
- Subprocessors (EU): See attached redwood-regions-subprocessor-list.pdf — includes compute partners, cloud egress points, and our telemetry vendor. All EU subprocessors are under EU data processing agreements and signatory to our SCC addendum where applicable.
- Cross-border triggers: By default we do NOT move EU-pinned requests outside the EU. Exceptions only occur under these narrow scenarios:
  1) Customer-configured multi-region routing (opt-in).
  2) Emergency failover when the EU pool is completely degraded and a customer has not configured strict region-isolation; in that case we will attempt same-day notification and remediation.
  3) Regulatory or lawful process requests where we are required by law to provide access.
You can opt out of (2) by enabling strict region-blocking in the account control plane — we'll include steps in the drive doc.
- Retention & deletion: Runtime KV caches and transient artifacts are ephemeral by default (TTL within seconds to hours depending on workload); the attached data-deletion-playbook.pdf lists retention windows and the erase flow for request traces and cached tensors. Customer-owned persistent artifacts (embeddings, stored prompts) follow configured retention policies and can be deleted via API or through the Console.

Attachments included: redwood-regions-subprocessor-list.pdf, data-deletion-playbook.pdf

Next steps: would you like a short 30‑minute call with Karthik to walk through the opt-out controls and a legal handoff for SCCs / DPA redlines?

Best,
Monica Patel
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Oliver Stone <oliver.stone@atlantech.com>

Subject: Re: Initial questions: execution loci, subprocessors, and cross-border triggers

Monica — thanks, helpful. A couple follow-ups from our infra team (copying Emma):

- On emergency failover: can you confirm how routing decisions are made? Is it automatic based on capacity, or do you require a manual escalation to route EU traffic to US pools?
- KMS question: if a customer pins to EU, are the KMS keys also region-bound (i.e., key material never leaves EU)?
- If we enable strict region-blocking, do you provide telemetry to confirm a request was served in EU (audit traces)?

If you can provide answers in writing before the call that would help speed legal review.

On the call logistics: lunch slots Tue/Wed are best for us.

—Oliver

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Stone <oliver.stone@atlantech.com>, Emma Jackson <emma.jackson@atlantech.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-14T14:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial questions: execution loci, subprocessors, and cross-border triggers

Hi Oliver / Emma — quick technical clarifications: 

1) Failover behaviour: routing decisions are automatic and policy-driven in our control plane. For EU-pinned accounts with default settings, we prefer local EU capacity; if the EU pool crosses a pre-configured health and capacity threshold (severe outage), the system will evaluate compatible variants and either queue, throttle, or route to a fallback region based on customer policy. Customers can select one of three policies: Strict (no cross-border), Local-prefer + Notify (automatic fallback + alert), or Cost-prefer (route to lowest-cost compatible region).

2) KMS and key residency: We integrate with customer-managed KMS (BYOK) and with cloud KMS providers. If you provision a customer-managed key in an EU KMS instance and bind it to the account, key material never leaves that KMS. For Redwood-managed keys, we store DEKs encrypted under region-scoped KMS keys; we can provide attestations for key wrapping locality on request.

3) Telemetry & audits: yes — when Strict region-blocking is enabled we emit audit traces that include execution-region, compute-node id, and subprocessor id. Those traces are retained according to the evidence retention policy (we can provide a filtered evidence pack on request).

I've attached an SLA exception form (sla-exception-request-form.xlsx) that legal sometimes uses for formalizing cross-border guarantees. We'll bring a tech + legal rep on the call if you like.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
